thread.title: Malea Joelle White - NewsBreak

author: Channel3000com News 3 Now
title: Malea Joelle White - NewsBreak
text:
1 days ago Malea Joelle White, aged 25, passed away peacefully on October 2, 2025, in her hometown of Madison, Wisconsin. Born on May 2, 2000, to Cynthia Palmer and Leonte White, Malea's life was a testament to love, courage, strength and advocacy. Her radiant spirit and unwavering dedication to making the world a better place for children in the foster care system will be deeply missed by all who knew her.
Malea spent a significant part of her childhood in California, and it always held a special place in her heart. She attended Sun Prairie High school and graduated from Memorial High School, where she was known for her vibrant personality. She furthered her education at Madison Area Technical College (MATC), where she honed her skills to become a formidable advocate for those without a voice. Malea's work took her across the country, where she attended conferences and engaged with lawmakers to drive meaningful change. Her passion for her vocation was evident in every speech delivered and every life she touched.
Her interests were as diverse as her talents - a lover of music, movies, she also cherished the moments spent with those she loved. Malea's creative energy found expression in her crocheting, painting, and writing, which not only brought beauty into the world but also served as a source of comfort and inspiration.
Malea is survived by her loving mother, Cynthia Palmer, and father, Leonte (Diane) White. Her memory will be cherished by her siblings Shaun White-Palmer, Micah Palmer, Leaf Anthony, Elijah Anthony, Lalonie White, LaSasha White, Javon White, and Usin Pierce. Malea's broad family circle includes many aunts, uncles, grandparents, and extended loved ones who will hold her in their hearts forever. She also leaves behind special friends Jazmine Field, Lexi Grasty and Tattionna Lyons, who were her confidants and companions on her life's path. Malea was preceded in death by her dear stepfather, Emmitt Palmer, who raised her with kindness as his own.
Malea's legacy is one of compassion, advocacy, and the indomitable spirit of youth. Her life may have been short, but the impact she made will resonate for generations to come. As we bid farewell to this remarkable young woman, we celebrate the light she brought into our lives and the difference she made in the world. Malea Joelle White will be remembered not only for the battles she fought but for the love she spread so freely. Her journey continues in the hearts of those who loved her, and her mission will endure through the countless lives she has influenced. Rest in peace, dear Malea. Your memory will be a beacon of hope and a reminder of the power of one person to make the world a better place.
Malea’s wake will be on Wednesday October 15th 11:30-12:30 at Foster Funeral Home.
